UnitStatement: AGENT_TASK.md defines TASK as the generic bounded-task shell instruction file.

TASK does not assume a specific document set, decomposition variant, or work method.
TASK normalizes the brief into a bounded task contract.
TASK loads any declared skill.
TASK executes requested work inside the authorized boundary.
TASK prefers deterministic tools where they help.
TASK returns an auditable run report.

Method variability belongs in deterministic tools under tools/.

An inline INIT-TASK brief can be passed directly in the invocation payload.
A file-based TASK brief can be provided at INIT-TASK.md.
When inline and file-based briefs are both present, TASK normalizes them into one effective brief using precedence rules.
Legacy deliverable fields are compatibility metadata only.

TaskProfile DELIVERABLE_TASK is accepted only as a deprecated compatibility label.
TaskProfile DELIVERABLE_TASK does not load a separate pathway.

AGENT_TASK.md is normative over AGENT_DELIVERABLE_TASK.md for TASK behavior.
Instruction files use AGENT_* names, while agents use role names.
TASK has AGENT_TYPE TYPE 2.
TASK has AGENT_CLASS TASK.
TASK uses INIT-TASK as its interaction surface.
TASK write scope is bounded-task-brief.
TASK is never blocking.
TASK primary outputs are a run record plus optional brief-defined or skill-defined outputs within authorized scope.
DELIVERABLE_TASK is a deprecated compatibility label with no active profile behavior.
When TaskProfile is omitted, TASK runs using AGENT_TASK.md plus any declared skill.
When TaskProfile DELIVERABLE_TASK is provided, TASK records it in the run report for compatibility.
When TaskProfile DELIVERABLE_TASK is provided, TASK does not load any separate behavior.
When TaskProfile DELIVERABLE_TASK is provided, TASK does not infer read or write permissions from the profile label.
An unsupported TaskProfile causes TASK to return ERROR: Unsupported TaskProfile=<value>.
TASK may read files needed to satisfy the effective bounded task brief.
TASK may use only tools permitted by the brief or active skill contract.
TASK writes only when explicitly authorized by the effective bounded task brief.
AllowedWriteTargets narrows write authorization to listed targets when present.
TASK creates and updates a run record file within ScopePath/_run_records/.
TASK must not edit files outside the effective bounded task brief write authorization.
TASK must not treat ScopePath, DeliverablePath, or TaskProfile as implicit write authorization.
TASK must not expand work into a different work root for convenience.
TASK must not invent facts, parameters, or outputs unsupported by the brief, skill, or evidence.
TASK must not let a skill or compatibility profile override the shell hard authorization boundary.
A TASK brief may contain generic fields, legacy fields, a file-based brief, or a combination of those forms.
InitTaskPath is an accepted field for an explicit path to a file-based INIT-TASK.md.
INIT_TASK_PATH is an uppercase alias for InitTaskPath.
ScopePath is the preferred run and context anchor.
ScopePath determines the run-record location.
DeliverablePath is a legacy compatibility field or skill-runtime input.
DeliverablePath does not activate a profile.

TaskSkill is an accepted TASK behavior field.
Tasks is an accepted TASK behavior field.
ApplyEdits is an accepted TASK behavior field.
AllowedWriteTargets is an accepted TASK behavior field.
AllowedTools is an accepted TASK behavior field.
RuntimeOverrides is an accepted TASK behavior field.
CustomInstructions is an accepted TASK behavior field.
ExpectedOutputs is an accepted TASK behavior field.
EXCLUSIONS is an accepted TASK behavior field.
TASK normalization determines whether a file-based brief exists.
If InitTaskPath or INIT_TASK_PATH is provided, TASK uses it as the file control surface.
If ScopePath is known and ScopePath/INIT-TASK.md exists, TASK uses that file when no explicit InitTaskPath is active.
If DeliverablePath is known and DeliverablePath/INIT-TASK.md exists, TASK can use that file when higher-priority file controls are absent.
If no file control source is found, no file control surface is active.
When a file control surface is active, TASK reads it first.
TASK interprets an active file control surface as a structured INIT-TASK brief using the same field names where possible.
TASK uses file-derived values only to fill fields omitted from the inline brief.
Inline fields are authoritative over file-derived fields.
If the same path field appears in inline and file-derived values but resolves differently, TASK returns an error for that field.
If DeliverablePath is present, TASK keeps it as a legacy compatibility field or skill input.
TASK does not set ScopePath from DeliverablePath unless ScopePath is absent.
TASK does not infer TaskProfile DELIVERABLE_TASK from DeliverablePath.
If TaskProfile is DELIVERABLE_TASK and DeliverablePath is absent, TASK continues with no special profile behavior.
If TaskProfile is DELIVERABLE_TASK and DeliverablePath is absent, TASK uses ScopePath only as the run and context anchor.
If ScopePath is absent after normalization and DeliverablePath is present, TASK sets ScopePath to DeliverablePath as a legacy fallback.
If ScopePath remains absent after normalization, TASK stops and returns ERROR: ScopePath is required.
If ScopePath does not resolve to an existing local path, TASK stops and returns ERROR: ScopePath does not exist.
If ScopePath and DeliverablePath are both provided and resolve differently, TASK allows the difference.
When ScopePath and DeliverablePath differ, ScopePath remains the run/context anchor and DeliverablePath remains legacy or skill input.
If InitTaskPath or INIT_TASK_PATH is provided but does not resolve to an existing file, TASK returns ERROR: InitTaskPath does not exist.
If AllowedWriteTargets is present, every target must resolve to an explicit local path or supported local path pattern.
AllowedWriteTargets forms a whitelist for non-run-record writes.
If AllowedTools is present, TASK uses only the listed tool paths plus reads required to load the shell and active skill contract.
If TaskSkill is provided, TASK first tries skills/{TaskSkill}/SKILL.md.
If TaskSkill contains underscores and the direct skill path does not exist, TASK tries a hyphenated compatibility alias.
When a compatibility skill alias is used, the hyphenated folder token becomes the canonical skill identity for the run.
When the resolved skill file exists, TASK loads it and follows it as a method contract.
A loaded skill method contract is subordinate to the effective bounded task brief write authorization.
A loaded skill method contract is subordinate to the TASK shell hard authorization boundary and run-record rules.
A loaded skill method contract is subordinate to explicit skill constraints that narrow or validate the run.
If the resolved TaskSkill file does not exist, TASK returns ERROR: TaskSkill not found.
After resolving a skill, TASK uses the resolved skill folder for all companion-file lookups.
Canonical repo-native skills must contain BRIEF_SCHEMA.md, TOOL_POLICY.md, and QA_CHECKS.md companion files.
If a required companion file is missing, TASK returns ERROR: TaskSkill companion files missing.
Notes: Potential internal tension with line 266, which says companion-file absence is reported with no error.

UnitStatement: When required skill companion files are present, TASK loads them alongside SKILL.md.
After resolving a skill folder, TASK parses SKILL.md YAML frontmatter.
TASK confirms the SKILL.md frontmatter name matches the resolved skill folder name.
If the skill frontmatter name does not match the resolved folder, TASK emits a warning and continues.
If skill allowed-tools is present, TASK parses it as a comma-space delimited list of command specs.
Each skill allowed-tools command spec must be exactly an interpreter, a repo-relative tool path, and a scope glob.
Skill allowed-tools command specs must not include flags or extra arguments.
Each skill allowed-tools tool path must resolve to an existing file under tools/.
Malformed or unresolvable skill allowed-tools causes TASK to return an error and stop.
If skill allowed-tools is absent, no skill-level tool restriction applies.
When both brief AllowedTools and skill allowed-tools are present, the effective tool allowlist is their intersection.
A brief cannot grant tools that the skill forbids.
A skill cannot grant tools that the brief forbids.
When only one source provides a tool allowlist, that source is the effective allowlist.
When neither source provides a tool allowlist, no tool restriction applies.
TASK records metadata.chirality-task-profile from SKILL.md frontmatter.
If metadata.chirality-task-profile is absent, TASK treats it as NONE.
Non-NONE chirality-task-profile values are deprecated compatibility metadata and do not load behavior or grant write authority.
TASK records metadata.chirality-skill-version from SKILL.md frontmatter.
If metadata.chirality-skill-version is absent, TASK records UNKNOWN.
Skill description and compatibility frontmatter fields are descriptive and are not machine-consumed.
Skills may define preferred tool usage.
Skills may define expected output structures.
Skills may define QA checks.
Skills may define sub-modes and runtime overrides.
Skills may define additional bounded read targets and method-specific read/write validation.
Skills must not widen write authority beyond the effective bounded task brief.
A skill may narrow write targets.
A skill may require stricter validation.
A skill may refuse an ambiguous brief.
TASK resolves write authorization from the effective bounded task brief after file/inline merge.
The run record at ScopePath/_run_records/TASK_RUN_*.md is always authorized by the TASK shell.
If ApplyEdits is absent or false, no non-run-record writes are authorized.
If ApplyEdits is absent or false, TASK returns proposals when useful.
If ApplyEdits is true and AllowedWriteTargets is present, non-run-record writes are limited to those targets.
If ApplyEdits is true and AllowedWriteTargets is absent, writes must match explicitly named writable files, directories, or artifact boundaries in the effective brief.
If the requested write boundary is ambiguous, TASK does not guess.
For an ambiguous write boundary, TASK stops with FAILED_INPUTS or reports NEEDS_HUMAN_RULING depending on whether useful analysis can continue without writes.
ScopePath, DeliverablePath, and TaskProfile are never sufficient write authorization by themselves.
Every TASK run must produce a durable run record at ScopePath/_run_records/TASK_RUN_{YYYY-MM-DD}_{HHmm}.md.
A TASK run record is a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter.
A TASK run record captures an input echo of the requested control surface, scope, profile, skill, tasks, and expected outputs.
A TASK run record captures resolved state for loaded skill path, version, companion files, effective tool policy, and overrides.
A TASK run record captures execution results including status, tools used, outputs, missing items, rulings needed, and changes.
At normalization, TASK creates a run record with run-status PENDING and populated input and resolved-state fields.
At completion, TASK updates the run record status to SUCCESS, FAILED, or FAILED_INPUTS and populates completion headings.
After the owning run completes, the run record is never modified.
If normalization fails before ScopePath is resolved, TASK writes no run record and returns the error in conversation only.
If the _run_records directory does not exist, TASK creates it.
If a run-record file with the same timestamp already exists, TASK appends a sequence number.
TASK structural validation collects checks enforced during normalization, method loading, QA, and protocol step 5.
Pre-execution validation requires the resolved skill folder to exist; failure stops with ERROR: TaskSkill not found.
Pre-execution validation requires skill allowed-tools paths to resolve to existing files under tools/.
Pre-execution validation records skill chirality-task-profile and treats non-NONE values as warnings without loading profile behavior.
Pre-execution validation requires AllowedWriteTargets to resolve to explicit local paths or supported local path patterns.
Pre-execution validation requires explicit write authorization when ApplyEdits is true.
Ambiguous write authorization with ApplyEdits true results in FAILED_INPUTS or NEEDS_HUMAN_RULING.
Companion files are explicitly checked and reported found or absent with no error on absence.
Notes: Potential internal tension with line 185, which says missing required companion files cause an error.

UnitStatement: Post-execution QA fails if files outside effective write authorization were modified.
Post-execution QA fails if tool usage violates an active declared allowlist.
Post-execution QA expects each tool used to be reported in interpreter-and-tool-path format.
Post-execution QA warns if a declared-first tool was not invoked first.
Post-execution QA fails if AllowedWriteTargets is present and writes occur outside its whitelist except run records.
Post-execution QA fails if AllowedWriteTargets is absent and non-run-record writes do not match explicit brief text.
Post-execution QA warns if required run-record YAML frontmatter fields are missing.
Post-execution QA warns if required run-record Markdown body headings are missing.
When a skill is loaded, TASK checks BRIEF_SCHEMA.md, TOOL_POLICY.md, and QA_CHECKS.md companion file slots.
TASK reports CompanionFiles as each companion filename with found or absent status, or none checked when no skill is loaded.
TaskProfile DELIVERABLE_TASK is accepted only so older briefs can still be parsed.
TaskProfile DELIVERABLE_TASK does not load AGENT_DELIVERABLE_TASK.md.
TaskProfile DELIVERABLE_TASK does not require or infer DeliverablePath.
TaskProfile DELIVERABLE_TASK does not load a deliverable truth set.

Deliverable-specific reads, memory updates, closeout fields, and artifact write rules must be stated in the effective brief or loaded skill contract.
Deliverable-specific rules remain subject to the brief write authorization.
TASK always operates as a generic bounded-task shell.
TASK must read only files needed to complete the stated tasks.
TASK must prefer deterministic tools for repeatable transformations and checks.
TASK must keep edits minimal and reversible.
TASK must return a structured run report even if no writes occurred.
The TASK shell does not imply any special memory file, document set, deliverable metadata convention, or project lifecycle convention.

TASK shell mechanics include run-record persistence.

TASK shell mechanics include write authorization checks.

Brief authority includes runtime parameters.
Brief authority includes custom instructions.

During normalization, TASK resolves ScopePath.
During normalization, TASK records deprecated compatibility labels when present.

TASK protocol step 4 executes within bounds.
During execution, TASK reads only files needed for the task.
During execution, TASK applies edits only when authorized.
During execution, TASK keeps all writes inside the resolved brief authorization.

During QA, TASK compares tool usage against any declared allowlist.
During QA, TASK confirms outputs match the requested shape as best as possible.
During QA, TASK verifies run-record structural completeness.
During QA, TASK updates the run record with final status and completion headings.
